_comment: DEPARTMENTAL POLICY, one file for the whole fleet.
The deploy script sets `group` per OU (or per machine) and every workstation
picks the matching overlay out of groupPolicies. One GPO, one artifact to
review, one file in change control -- instead of eleven near-identical
policy files that drift apart within a quarter.
WHY DEPARTMENTS NEED DIFFERENT RULES AT ALL
A single fleet-wide configuration has to be set for the strictest
population, which means everyone else lives with false positives. The
README already names the consequence: 'a tool that blocks legitimate work
gets uninstalled or worked around within a week.' They cannot uninstall a
force-installed extension -- so instead they use their phone, and you have
traded a logged event for an invisible one. That is a worse outcome than
Overlay semantics: a group overlay is merged ON TOP of the baseline, so it
only needs to state its differences. Objects merge key-by-key; arrays

_why: County Attorney. Privileged material, active litigation, sealed
records. Strict means warn-severity findings block too, and an
uninspectable attachment is refused rather than flagged -- for this
group 'we could not read the PDF' is not an acceptable outcome.
Personnel files, discipline, medical and benefits data. Same posture
as legal, except HR genuinely lives in Workday all day -- which is
already in neverScan, so nothing here needs to loosen for it.
CJIS applies. The cjis and cjis_id rules exist for this group above
all others, and the FBI CJIS Security Policy makes disclosure to a
third-party service a reportable event, not a policy preference.
Note media_ai is enforced here rather than warned: an investigator
uploading a suspect photo to an image tool is a real scenario and it
is not one to leave to a confirm dialog.
HIPAA covered functions. The medical rule is warn-severity by default
because the vocabulary is noisy in general office use -- but in this
department a prompt containing 'patient' and 'diagnosis' is exactly
what needs stopping, so strict promotes it to a block.
The one group with a legitimate, daily need to paste text that trips
internal_host: stack traces, config files, subnet plans. Exempting
that ONE rule for this group is the difference between a tool they
use and a tool they route around.
Note what is NOT exempted: credential and private_key stay live. An
API key in a paste is the highest-value thing this tool catches, and
IT is the group most likely to paste one.
code_ai is warn rather than enforce because pasting a snippet into a
coding assistant is the job. The warn step still logs it.
Parcel and address data is largely public record in Texas. The
case_number and dob rules fire constantly on parcel exports and
survey dates, and neither is a disclosure here.
Public information office. Their job is producing material intended
for release, and gov_email fires on every press contact they write.
Warn mode across the board: log everything, interrupt rarely.
Everyone not in a named group. Deliberately the baseline and nothing
more -- if a department needs an exception, give it a group so the
exception is visible in change control rather than quietly widening
the default for the whole county.
Rollout group. Monitor everything, block nothing, stage everything.
Run a department here for two weeks BEFORE enforcing on it, then read
the morning report and count how many blocks would have been false
positives. That number is the single most useful thing you can bring
to the meeting where someone asks whether this is ready.
